newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares show no sign of ending record gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares show no sign of ending record gains.

text.p: German shares, gaining strength from the dollar and the Wall Street advance, appeared set to keep up their record advance after hitting another new record high in active bourse dealings on Monday.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 59.87 points at 3,436.07 points but pared some of the gains in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings to trade at 3,419.14 points.
Despite the bout of profit-taking, some market participants said the DAX index was not ready for a correction.
"I think the market still definitely has room to go higher," said one Frankfurt trader.

The initial public offering in shares in German mobile phone service provider Mobilcom AG, which will trade on the Neue Markt, were more than 100 times oversubscribed, its chief executive Gerhard Schmid told Reuters on Monday.
The share market was gearing up for a rash of corporate information this week, with the three big chemical companies all due to report this week and next week.
Results for 1996 are due on Tuesday from Hoechst AG and Bayer AG. BASF AG will report its figures next week.
"There are still a lot of areas in the market that are showing good value," he said.
But few traders said the market would leap toward 3,500 points anytime soon, saying the level was set as a target for the summer but would now likely be reached in early April.
Among the gainers was engineering group Deutz AG after reports last week that the group would report a profit next year. Deutz was up 1.60 marks at 12.40 marks.

Monday was also the opening day for trade in Frankfurt's new market for technology, new media and other growth stocks, the Neue Markt, modelled on New York's Nasdaq index. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
